title: Procurement pathways and SLA matrix experiment for isolated/private deployments
creator: Marcela Ruiz
description: Goal: validate two complementary packaging approaches for Private/VPC and on-prem customers (a simple bundled license+support SKU and a modular procurement path that allows add-on support, accelerated upgrades, and optional managed services). We will run sales-led pilots with 3 anchor prospects and an internal simulated procurement funnel to measure time-to-sign, ACV, and legal/security friction. This ticket covers the PRD for SKU definitions, SLA matrix, SOW/contract templates, security questionnaire mapping, and the experiment plan for measuring commercial outcomes. Background: customers frequently ask for clearer upgrade cadences and explicit repair/patch SLAs for air-gapped installs. Sales reports high friction from multi-line-item quotes and unclear scope for upgrade services. Engineering warns about on-prem upgrades during maintenance windows and KMS rotation constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 SKU archetypes (Core License + Basic Support, Premium License + Priority Support, Enterprise License + Managed Upgrade Option) with pricing bands and renewal terms
Publish an SLA matrix that maps support tier to response/repair/upgrade cadence and measurable SLOs for uptime/patch turnaround
Create an SOW template and contract language for upgrade windows, rollback support, and data handling for on-prem installs
Complete security questionnaire mapping for the top 20 buyer questions and attach required artifacts (KMS/HSM details, audit log retention, upgrade checklist)
Run 3 sales pilots and capture metrics: time-to-sign, ACV change vs baseline, number of legal iterations, and security questionnaire completion time
Deliver a go/no-go recommendation and a recommended rollout plan to pricing council
